key_insight: A recurrent Structural Policy Gradient algorithm lets agents in partially observable Mean Field Games learn scalable, low-variance policies by combining exact structural expectations with Monte Carlo treatment of common (aggregate) noise and a recurrent memory for hidden information.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-variance model-free approaches and computationally costly exact methods for large-population games under partial observability: it enables tractable, sample-efficient learning when agents only observe local/partial signals and the population introduces common shocks.
method: Hybrid structural decomposition: compute exact expectations over idiosyncratic effects while using Monte Carlo rollouts for common (aggregate) noise to keep computations tractable.

Recurrent policy-gradient: parameterize agents with recurrent policies (RNNs/LSTMs) to capture partial observability and history-dependent strategies while applying a structural policy gradient update.
Variance-reduction & scalability: exploit mean-field structure to reduce estimator variance and scale to large populations without fully enumerating joint dynamics.
impact: Provides a practical, lower-variance approach for training policies in large multi-agent settings with hidden state and aggregate shocks, improving sample efficiency and enabling deployment of principled MFG methods in real-world domains (e.g., economics, traffic, resource allocation).
visual_elements: Schematic of a single agent interacting with the population mean-field: incoming partial observations → recurrent policy → action; arrows show feedback to mean-field.
Algorithm flowchart: hybrid exact expectation block + Monte Carlo common-noise rollouts + recurrent policy-gradient update.
Performance plot: sample-efficiency or variance comparison vs model-free and exact baselines (learning curve / error bars).
Illustration of partial observability: timeline showing hidden common shocks inferred via recurrent memory vs naive memoryless policies.
paper_title: Recurrent Structural Policy Gradient for Partially Observable Mean Field Games
paper_authors: Clarisse Wibault, Johannes Forkel, Sebastian Towers, Tiphaine Wibault, Juan Duque
